items.title: Bob Wilber Interview, 1961-05-01
items.q: The interviewee (Bob Wilber) responds to the interviewer's mention of John Reed by discussing Sidney Bechet's musical style and habits. There is no direct statement from Bob Wilber indicating a personal relationship, meeting, or collaboration with John Reed.

ctx.x: Ballet, yeah, which later was produced. This was when he was really working on it.

I remember 1944, I was once up in Harlem with John Reed to see him in the basement apartment where he had a piano and he got out the score and played it. He played not too well on piano, actually, as you know, I guess.

He loved to sit at the piano and play. And he had his own distinctive harmonic idiom in his tunes. It was limited, but he had certain progressions which were unusual that you could identify with Sidney. They say, yeah, that's one of Sidney's progressions.

items.title: Bob Wilber Interview, 1961-05-01
items.q: Yes I know I knew of him I never met him yeah.

ctx.x: used played the clarinet a lot. He played the clarinet in those days. He loved to play the clarinet except on a job he was always a little afraid of it because he couldn't express himself as freely on the clarinet it was a little more delicate you know but at home he loved to sit and play the clarinet.
Oh do you remember anything about his clarinet? I know he gave one of them once when he sort of gave up he had trouble with his teeth he gave one to John Reed's wife you knew John Reed I
suppose had been connected. Yes I know I knew of him I never met him yeah. Remember that was 1943
